Zaliztsi Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ternopil Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Zaliztsi's Jewish community, first documented with 80 people in 1606, was destroyed during the Cossack invasion of 1648–54 and revived by the late 17th century. Across the following centuries it was served by named rabbis including Israel Zak, Eliezer Horowitz, and Menachem-Mendl Kagane. A Baron Hirsch-supported school taught 118 students by 1895. The population, once 2,412 (34.8 percent of the town) in 1890, had collapsed to just 524 (10.9 percent) by 1921. Nearly 20 Jews were murdered on the first day of the German occupation in July 1941; the few survivors who returned in 1945 soon left again, for Poland.
